title: Minimum Cost to Reach City With Discounts
summary: Given a network of n cities connected by highways with associated tolls, and a certain number of discounts, determine the least cost to travel from city 0 to city n-1.
statement: Given a network of n cities connected by highways with associated tolls, and a certain number of discounts, determine the least cost to travel from city 0 to city n-1. Use at most one discount per highway to halve the toll cost, and return -1 if the journey is impossible.
constraints: Highways are undirected and have nonnegative integer tolls.
Each available discount may halve one traversed toll using floor division; using fewer discounts is allowed.
Return the minimum cost from city zero to city n-1, or -1 when unreachable.
hints: The same city with different numbers of discounts used represents different future choices.
Run Dijkstra on states (city,used), relaxing every highway at full cost and, if available, half cost.
Maintain dist[n][discounts+1] and a min-heap; return when any destination state is popped.
All expanded edge weights are nonnegative, so Dijkstra finalizes the globally cheapest destination state first.
editorial: All expanded edge weights are nonnegative, so Dijkstra finalizes the globally cheapest destination state first.

tests.explanation: Discounting toll eleven to five yields total cost nine.
Discounting both highways costs two plus two, totaling four.
